introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b), your name must be Kassala and your address Lycée de Mololo.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the events in the pictures.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

questions.corrige_markdown:
**The six pictures ("Un garçon tombe d'un arbre"), in order**

1. A boy lies along a branch of a big tree and stretches his arm towards some fruit (mangoes) at the end of the branch.
2. The branch breaks with a crack and the boy falls head first towards the ground; some fruit has already fallen on the grass.
3. The boy lies on his back on the ground in full daylight (the sun is high) beside the broken branch and the fruit.
4. The sun is setting; the boy sits on the ground holding his injured leg, with the broken branch lying nearby.
5. It is almost dark; the boy is still sitting on the ground while someone comes running towards him with raised arms.
6. A woman stands at the door of a house with her arms open as a man arrives carrying the boy.

**Tense chosen:** the passé composé for the events, with the imparfait for the scene and the boy's feelings. A past tense is needed because the story is told after the events.

**Model essay** (142 words)

Un après-midi, un garçon est monté sur un grand arbre pour cueillir des mangues, car il avait très faim. Il s'est avancé prudemment sur une branche, mais elle a cassé sous son poids avant qu'il atteigne les fruits.

Le garçon est tombé brutalement par terre, la jambe tordue. Il s'est fait très mal à la jambe et il ne pouvait plus se lever. Il est resté là plusieurs heures. Le soleil se couchait, puis la nuit est arrivée, et il avait peur.

Heureusement, un homme qui passait par là a entendu ses cris. Il a couru vers lui et il l'a pris dans ses bras. Il l'a porté jusqu'à la maison de ses parents.

Sa mère l'attendait inquiète devant la porte et elle l'a serré dans ses bras. Le garçon a promis de ne plus jamais grimper sur un arbre sans prudence.

**Notes**

The answer covers the three bullet points: why the boy climbed the tree (to pick fruit, pictures 1-2), what happened to him (the branch broke, he fell and was hurt, pictures 2-4), who helped him, when and how (a passer-by, at nightfall, carried him home, pictures 5-6). The woman at the door in picture 6 is taken to be his mother; this is an interpretation of the pictures.

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All three bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Telling a story that does not follow the pictures (off-topic material earns no marks).
2. Describing each picture one by one ("Dans l'image 1...") instead of telling a connected story.
